expectations.text: Flags the column rename as breaking old pods during the ~15-min rolling window (they still query full_name)
expectations.evidence: Finding 2: 'From that moment until the last v1 pod terminates (~15 minutes), every v1 pod still in the rollout executes SELECT ... full_name ... / UPDATE ... SET full_name = ... against a schema where the column no longer exists. Every one of those queries errors — column "full_name" does not exist. That's up to 15 minutes of hard failures.'

expectations.text: Notes the rename also breaks rollback to the previous release even after the rollout completes
expectations.evidence: Intro states the schema must stay compatible 'plus however long you need rollback to v1 to remain possible afterwards'; Finding 2: 'And rollback is worse than the rollout: if v2 misbehaves and you redeploy v1, v1 is now broken by the schema, so rolling back the application requires also reverse-renaming the column — under incident pressure, against data v2 has been writing.' Not scoped to mid-rollout only.

expectations.text: Flags VARCHAR(100)->VARCHAR(20) narrowing as silently irreversible: truncated values are not restored by widening back
expectations.evidence: Finding 1: 'Narrowing VARCHAR(100) → VARCHAR(20) discards information. Widening back later restores the *shape* of the column, not any characters that were lost — there is no down migration for this.' Also flags MySQL non-strict mode 'silently truncates ... one of them is invisible.'

expectations.text: Recommends verifying existing phone values fit the new length before narrowing (data check, not assumption)
expectations.evidence: Finding 1: '"We checked" is a point-in-time observation, not a constraint'; recommends 'add a CHECK (char_length(phone) <= 20) NOT VALID, clean existing data, then VALIDATE CONSTRAINT'; replacement step 4: 'Verify with queries: ... zero phones over 20 chars ... Then VALIDATE CONSTRAINT on the phone check.'

expectations.text: Flags NOT NULL loyalty_tier without a default as breaking inserts from old pods mid-rollout
expectations.evidence: Finding 3 flags the statement failing outright on existing rows, then: 'If you "fix" it by adding a DEFAULT, it's still only conditionally safe: it works because v1's inserts (which don't mention loyalty_tier) get the default — but that means "v2 sets it on every insert" is doing none of the safety work; the default is.' Explicitly identifies old-pod inserts as incompatible with NOT NULL absent a default.

expectations.text: Proposes a staged multi-deployment alternative (Expand-Migrate-Contract or equivalent) instead of merging as-is
expectations.evidence: Verdict is 'do not merge'; Finding 2 gives a 5-step 'Staged alternative (Expand–Migrate–Contract), each step an independent deployment'; the 'Recommended shape of the replacement' section lays out a 6-step deployment sequence (expand V42, dual-write app deploy, backfill, verify, contract app deploy, later V43+ cleanup).

expectations.text: Recommends delaying destructive cleanup (dropping full_name) past a rollback window with verification first
expectations.evidence: Finding 2 step 5: 'Cleanup (separate, later migration, after the rollback window and after proving nothing reads/writes full_name): drop full_name. This is the only irreversible step, which is why it goes last and alone, with a date and an owner.' Replacement step 6: 'V43+, after an agreed rollback window (put a date on it now): drop full_name.'

claims.claim: On Postgres, narrowing a varchar forces a full table rewrite under an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock, unlike widening which is metadata-only
claims.evidence: Consistent with PostgreSQL behavior: increasing varchar typmod is metadata-only since 9.2; decreasing requires ACCESS EXCLUSIVE with a table scan/rewrite.

claims.claim: NOT NULL with no DEFAULT fails outright on a non-empty table with 'column ... contains null values'
claims.evidence: Correct for PostgreSQL and strict-mode MySQL; the quoted error message matches Postgres.

claims.claim: On Postgres 11+, adding a column with a constant default is metadata-only (no rewrite)
claims.evidence: Correct; PG 11 introduced fast column addition with non-volatile defaults.

claims.claim: On PG 12+, a validated CHECK (col IS NOT NULL) constraint lets SET NOT NULL skip the full-table scan
claims.evidence: Correct; PG 12 uses an existing validated constraint to prove non-nullness.

claims.claim: Flyway wraps V42 in a single transaction on Postgres, so one failing statement fails the whole file
claims.evidence: Correct; Flyway runs each migration in a transaction on databases with transactional DDL such as Postgres.
